title: Strat Chat - Cold Call
author: Shaun Brien
summary: Brien argues that classroom participation is too often optional, so one reliable student answers while everyone else passively avoids learning, and that cold calling is the fix. He first lists the ways cold calling goes wrong and poisons culture: calling on inattentive students as punishment, naming the student before the question, too little wait time, accepting I don't know as final, and picking at random. He then lays out a precise procedure in which the teacher samples understanding with mini whiteboards or turn-and-talk, re-poses the question, waits at least four seconds, names a student, and echoes the answer. The warmth of a cold call, he says, comes from the lack of randomness, so the technique becomes a way to set students up for success.
points: The real problem is not the question but that participation is optional, and if it feels optional it is optional.
Five named misuses (behavior cold calls, name-first, short wait time, accepting I don't know, random picking) are the mutations that sour a cold call.
Pairing the question with mini-whiteboard sampling or turn-and-talk lets the teacher pick a student who can succeed, which makes the call warm.
The sequence is explicit: pose, sample, re-pose, pause at least four seconds, name, echo, then praise or probe.
Done well, every student thinks hard about content and gets a positive feedback loop.
quotes: The problem isn’t the teaching, it’s not even asking questions. It is the fact that participation is optional.
A ‘cold call’ question refers to asking for a response from a ‘non-volunteer’.

Saying the students name before the question - this gives every other student the signal that they can switch off as they no longer need to think as the question couldn’t possibly apply to or benefit them in their learning.
the average wait time of a teacher is less than one second before either answering it themselves or asking follow up questions.
The warmth in a cold call comes from the lack of randomness. As teachers we are using this as a tool to set students up for success.
Once the student answers the teacher then echoes back the students response to ensure the whole class hears what they have said.
